threads.body: The changelog attributes this deprecation to #19459, but the PR description says #19459 was the accidentally merged predecessor that this pull request replaces. Update this link to the current pull request so release notes do not point readers to the superseded change.

replies.body:
Addressed in d3a19d76e3a7e2c8e76068a9e38b1fa0d5c65358.

Analysis: PR #19495 replaces the accidentally merged predecessor, so its changelog entry should attribute the deprecation to the current pull request rather than #19459.

Upsides: Release-note readers are directed to the authoritative pull request and its final implementation context.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: The `selector == null` part is confusing for me. If the code reaches here I'd expect it to have something in the included list as otherwise we might add stuff to empty includes. Since empty includes mean include all adding items there would actually be restricting what is included. Doesn't `selector == null` mean no jfr metrics? If that is the case wouldn't it be better to return `null` straight away?
